methodological_questions: Can opponent next-possession PPP after a play type be reliably measured from play-by-play data?
Is opponent next-possession PPP a robust criterion for assigning AVOID labels to plays?
What are the risks of lookahead/leakage when using next possession outcome to label?

historical_evidence.finding: Superstar sequential suppression: PUTBACK is top suppressor for 6+ stars (D. Mitchell 1.178->0.884, d=-0.294, n_after=95; B. Beal d=-0.345 n=32; C. Holmgren d=-0.222 n=52). Other tops: TRANSITION, POST_UP. No multiplicity correction; n_after small.

Q5c verdict 'rank-1 suppressor varies meaningfully across players'; e.g. Jokic after opp POST_UP 1.1271 (-0.0675, SE ±0.0500, n=480); Curry forced POST_UP -0.209. Rank-1 deltas mostly within 1-2 SE with no multiple-comparison control.

Running play type X raises the same team's next 1-5 possession PPP vs matched baseline. Global horizons: DRIVE/SPOT_UP/TRANSITION=5; others 0. SPOT_UP lag-1 lift +0.027 ctrl_p=0.0000. Within-team: all horizons 0 except SPOT_UP horizon(all)=1; PNR lag-1 within_team_lift=-0.0218.

Extended Possession Value (direct PPP + opponent T+1 suppression). 4/8 PTs downstream real: CUT Ext 1.658 (supp +0.0220), TRANSITION 1.509 (+0.0145), SPOT_UP 1.303 (+0.0124), POST_UP 1.127 (+0.0194). DRIVE downstream not real (opp ATT +0.0024). Player downstream mostly BH ns.

Sequential pair premium and defensive aftershock (8/8 PTs). After opponent runs PT X, next offensive PT Y scores above Y's unconditional baseline. Aftershock 8/8 PTs replicate (CUT +0.119 n=21,398 / PO +0.131 n=1,145; TRANSITION +0.135 n=26,262 / +0.126 n=1,529). Top pair premiums PUTBACK->TRANSITION +0.084 n=565. Small sample limitation.

Play-type labeling audit: OTHER: 36% end in fouls, PPP inflated. DRIVE: 12pp below foul benchmark. PNR shows 22% foul rate. Only 335 of 50,668 possessions (0.7%) map to a real play type via initiation_type.

Persistent Impact Score Level 1 gate: FAIL decay-sanity; DRIVE lifts +0.015,+0.020,+0.018,+0.021,+0.020 (flat). Within-team: DRIVE lag-1 +0.015 to -0.002. Cohen d ~0.01-0.03; p~0 from n>150k. Callable play-type horizons = 0.
Season stability of top suppressors: only 2/30 (7%) stars stable (>=75% same top suppressor) across seasons. Negative teammate pairs e.g. Tatum->Porzingis DRIVE->SPOT_UP -0.444 n=31.

52-series sequential adaptation: durable_branches=[]. Median net swing: CUT +0.36 (neg in 9%), TRANSITION +0.26 (21%), PULL_UP +0.09 (33%), PNR +0.04 (45%), SPOT_UP +0.02 (40%), POST_UP -0.22 (77%), DRIVE -0.27 (88%). n_units: CUT 103, DRIVE/POST_UP/SPOT_UP lower.

Brown-initiated possession -> Tatum next-possession ATT. ATT near zero (PSM ATT=-0.0165, 95% CI [-0.0924,+0.0605]; exact-match ATT=-0.0857). Real ATT inside placebo range. Signs flip across quarters/RS-PO.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Measuring own-sequence action memory (own-sequence lags) globally.
failed_approaches.why: Flat non-decaying lifts disappear after within-team demeaning; team-quality confound produced artifact.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Persistent Impact Score Level 1 gate for own-sequence lags.
failed_approaches.why: Flat non-decaying lifts collapse under within-team baseline; team-quality confound.
Only 0.7% of possessions map to a real play type via initiation_type; foul leakage inflates/deflates PPP for OTHER and DRIVE.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Demonstrating stable top suppressors across seasons.
failed_approaches.why: Only 7% of stars have stable top suppressor; adequately powered null.

failed_approaches.what_failed: Finding durable pivot branches and meaningful net swing per play type.
failed_approaches.why: No conditional pivot branch met the durability bar; DRIVE/POST_UP negative net swings absent durable branches.

evidence_establishes: Opponent next-possession PPP rises detectably above an unconditional baseline for all eight major play types (defensive aftershock ~+0.12 PPP, SF07).
With rigorous matching the downstream suppression for four of eight play types remains real but is an order of magnitude smaller (~0.01-0.02 PPP; SF-APPS-075).

Own-sequence lags (action memory) that appear globally are entirely an artifact of team-quality confounding; within-team the memory vanishes except perhaps for a tiny SPOT_UP lag-1 (SF-APPS-073, SF-CHT-029).
Play-type labels derived from initiation_type are severely incomplete and contaminated (SF-CHT-025).
The specific suppressor play types that drive opponent next-PPP reductions for individual stars are not stable across seasons (SF-APPA-058).
evidence_does_not_establish: That opponent next-PPP effects are large enough (in magnitude) to be practically useful for defining AVOID labels.
That any own-sequence lag remains after proper within-team, game-state conditioning.
That AVOID labels based on these downstream effects would be stable or actionable, given the lack of durable play-type net swing patterns.
That the play-type labeling pipeline can currently produce a sufficient volume of reliably labeled possessions for this test.
own_inferences: The question requires two components: (a) opponent next-PPP effects large enough to motivate AVOID labels; (b) own-sequence lags also matter. The evidence shows that (a) exists but the effects are modest (0.01-0.12 PPP) and (b) is likely entirely artifact.

Given that the reliable downstream effects are ~0.01-0.02 PPP after matching, they are probably too small relative to the noise and the unreliability of the labels to serve as a robust criterion for AVOID classification.

If the AVOID labeling is based on raw global differences without within-team demeaning or matching, the labels will simply re-discover team-quality and game-context confounds rather than pure play-type effects.
A test of 'large enough' would need a pre-specified minimal effect size of practical importance (e.g., delta > 0.05 PPP) and would likely be unsupported or reject the hypothesis.
uncertainties: The exact mapping success rate of the play-type labeling for 'play X' in the question may differ from the 0.7% figure, but no evidence suggests it has been resolved since SF-CHT-025.
Whether AVOID labels would be defined per play type globally or per player-play-type pair, and what threshold of 'large enough' is intended.
Possible improvements to labeling (e.g., using alternative sources) could raise the usable sample size, but no record shows such improvement on this data.

historical_effect.explanation: Without the historical record one might assume that opponent next-PPP effects are large and own-sequence lags are real, making a labeling study plausible. The record shows that own-sequence lags are artifact, the reliable downstream effects are very small (~0.01-0.02 PPP), the play-type labels themselves are severely compromised, and top suppressors are unstable. This shifts the decision from 'proceed with careful design' to 'do not proceed' unless labeling is fundamentally repaired.

blocking_constraints.text: Play-type labels from initiation_type map only 0.7% of possessions, with substantial foul leakage inflating/deflating PPP for major play types.
Own-sequence lags are dominated by team-quality and game-context confounding; no residual real signal after within-team demeaning.

Even opponent next-PPP suppression effects are small (~0.01-0.02 PPP in matched analyses) relative to label noise and PPP variance, making it unlikely that a 'large enough' threshold will be reliably exceeded.
Rare play types and individual star-play-type suppressor cells often have small n (32-95) leading to imprecise estimates.

prior_work.summary: Multiple study families have already examined opponent next-PPP (defensive aftershock) and own-sequence lags. The opponent effects are real but modest; own-sequence lags are artifact. Play-type labeling is unreliable. No previous work has directly constructed AVOID labels from these effects, but the observed magnitudes and label quality strongly suggest the approach as posed is not viable.

risks.text: Only 0.7% of possessions are correctly mapped via initiation_type; foul-driven PPP inflation/deflation systematically biases play-type PPP estimates.
Own-sequence lag effects are fully confounded by team quality and game script; no real effect remains after within-team controls.
Opponent next-PPP effects are at the 0.01-0.02 PPP scale, making them highly sensitive to measurement noise and unlikely to produce stable AVOID labels.
Many relevant sub-groups (specific play types, player combinations) have fewer than 100 observations, preventing reliable effect estimation.
If AVOID labels are defined by extreme opponent next-PPP outcomes, regression to the mean will produce apparent stability decay absent proper correction.
The natural PPP variance across possessions is large; the separable signal from opponent suppression is a small fraction, making any 'large' label driven mostly by noise.

design.estimand: For each play type X, the difference in opponent next-possession PPP between possessions correctly labeled as X and matched control possessions not X, within the same team-season and narrow game-state strata.
design.unit: A single opponent possession immediately following a reliably labeled team possession.
design.sample: All regular season and playoff games 2022-23 through 2025-26 that can be successfully labeled via a repaired play-type pipeline (target >80% mapping success).
design.power: Minimum detectable effect of 0.03 PPP with 80% power after adjusting for 8 play types and within-team matching; requires >100,000 labeled possessions per common play type. Not achievable with current 0.7% labeling yield.
design.controls: Exact match on score margin (binned ≤±2 points), period, possession number remainder, opponent defensive rating, home/away; within-team demeaning to remove team-quality confound.
design.falsification: Own-sequence lag-1 effect must be indistinguishable from zero after controls. Known placebo test: effect should disappear when next-possession label is shuffled within the same period and margin bin.
design.multiplicity: Bonferroni correction for 8 primary play-type tests (threshold p < 0.00625).
design.decision_rule: Classify a play type X as 'AVOID-eligible' if the lower bound of the 95% CI for opponent next-PPP increase is ≥ 0.05 PPP, absent any sign of artifact in the falsification test.
design.data_version: NBA API per-game files frozen as of 2026-06-19; play-by-play parsed with the pipeline version that achieves <5% foul leakage and >80% valid initiation coverage.
